title: Full-Stack Web Developer
summary: Full-stack developers build both the part of a website people see and the server and database behind it. The role suits students who like seeing a whole product come together and are happy to keep learning across many tools.

sources.title: Full Stack Developer Roadmap – roadmap.sh

CS50's Web Programming with Python and JavaScript

nodes.title: How the web and HTTP work
nodes.summary: Learn what happens when you open a web page: browsers, servers, requests, responses, status codes and headers. Every later topic, from forms to APIs, builds on this.

resources.title: How the web works – MDN Web Docs
Overview of HTTP – MDN Web Docs

nodes.proof: Use your browser's network tab to explain, in your own words, every request a simple page makes and what each status code means.

sources.title: 8 In-Demand Full Stack Developer Skills – roadmap.sh

nodes.title: HTML, CSS and responsive layouts
nodes.summary: Write semantic HTML and style it with CSS, including Flexbox, Grid and layouts that work on phones. Clean, accessible markup is the base of every web job.

resources.title: Full Stack JavaScript Path – The Odin Project

nodes.proof: Build a responsive, multi-section landing page that looks right at phone and desktop widths, and host its code on GitHub.

sources.title: Full Stack Developer Roadmap – roadmap.sh
MDN Curriculum

nodes.title: JavaScript in depth
nodes.summary: Learn modern JavaScript well: functions, objects, arrays, the DOM, events, promises and async/await, and fetching data. It runs in the browser and, with Node.js, on the server too.

resources.title: Full Stack JavaScript Path – The Odin Project

nodes.proof: Build an interactive to-do or quiz app in plain JavaScript that saves data in the browser and loads data from a public API.

sources.title: 8 In-Demand Full Stack Developer Skills – roadmap.sh

nodes.title: Git and GitHub
nodes.summary: Use Git for every project: commits, branches, merges and pull requests. Teams expect it from day one, and your GitHub history is part of your portfolio.

resources.title: The Missing Semester of Your CS Education – MIT

nodes.proof: All your projects live on GitHub with small, clearly worded commits, and at least one used a branch and a merged pull request.

sources.title: Full Stack Developer Roadmap – roadmap.sh

nodes.title: One frontend framework (React)
nodes.summary: Learn one framework properly rather than several a little. React is a common choice: components, props, state, effects and routing. Focus on building, not on chasing every new library.

resources.title: Full Stack JavaScript Path – The Odin Project
CS50's Web Programming with Python and JavaScript

nodes.proof: Rebuild your plain JavaScript app in React with at least three routes and components that share state.

sources.title: 8 In-Demand Full Stack Developer Skills – roadmap.sh

nodes.title: Backend with Node.js and Express
nodes.summary: Write a server that exposes a REST API: routes, middleware, input validation and error handling. Using JavaScript on both sides lets you reuse what you already know.
nodes.proof: Build a REST API for notes or tasks with create, read, update and delete routes, and test each route with an HTTP client.

sources.title: Full Stack JavaScript Path – The Odin Project
Full Stack Developer Roadmap – roadmap.sh

nodes.title: SQL databases with PostgreSQL
nodes.summary: Learn tables, keys, joins, indexes and how to model data for an app. Connect your API to a real database instead of keeping data in memory.

resources.title: CS50's Introduction to Databases with SQL (archived, free to view)

nodes.proof: Design a schema with at least three related tables for your API and write queries that use joins and an index.

sources.title: Full Stack JavaScript Path – The Odin Project
8 In-Demand Full Stack Developer Skills – roadmap.sh

nodes.title: Login and web security basics
nodes.summary: Add sign-up and login safely: hash passwords with a slow algorithm, manage sessions, and check permissions on every request. Learn the most common web security risks so you avoid them by habit.
nodes.proof: Add login to your app with hashed passwords, and show that one user cannot read or change another user's data.

sources.title: OWASP Top 10:2025
Password Storage Cheat Sheet – OWASP

nodes.title: Build and deploy a full-stack app
nodes.summary: Combine everything into one app that real people can use online: React frontend, Express API, PostgreSQL database and login. Learning Docker helps you run the same setup everywhere.
nodes.proof: A live link and a public repo for an app with login, a database and at least one feature you designed yourself, plus a clear README.

nodes.title: Portfolio, interviews and applying
nodes.summary: Put your best two or three projects in a simple portfolio, tidy your GitHub and resume, and learn the usual hiring steps: phone screen, technical interview and take-home task. Apply steadily and follow up.
